verdict: OK to lend in Mangaluru shrimp processing — back the hygienic, multi-market processors with tight working-capital control; decline the ice-dependent, single-buyer, chemical-shortcut operators.
title: Mangaluru Seafood / Shrimp Processing & Export: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
Value sits in the cold chain and the buyer relationship, not in the plant. **The ice and water used to preserve fish are part of the product, not a utility** — the Dakshina Kannada food safety team inspected ice units at the Mangaluru fishing harbour and collected water samples, instructing owners to obtain lab test reports of the water used before continuing production [2]. A formalin warning was issued in the same drive [1]. So when a proposal lands, check the borrower's ice source and water test reports first; if they buy ice from tanker-fed units with no lab report, ask for the test certificate before you sanction. ## Where cash and value sit
**Working capital is the loan, and utilisation is the tell.** One peer processor ran maximum fund-based working-capital utilisation at about 96% for the twelve months ended June 30, 2025, and took temporary overdrafts from existing lenders [10]. That is the shape of a stressed account in this trade. Pricing power is thin and set abroad: Apex Frozen Foods held revenue flat at INR257 crores in Q1 FY27 versus INR258 crores a year earlier, yet PAT rose 138% to INR22 crores on a 15% increase in average shrimp realisation and US demand [5][6]. **Margin came from realisation, not volume** — so when a proposal lands, check the realisation assumption; if the projection assumes volume growth with flat prices, ask for the buyer-wise price sheet. ## What has changed now
**The rating view has turned, and it is recent.** CRISIL expects India's shrimp exports to exceed Rs 50,000 crore this fiscal, up 13-15% on-year after three years of stagnation, with rupee depreciation aiding realisations and margins steady [9]. That is a March 2026 report and supersedes the May 2025 view of flattish volumes and margin pressure from US tariffs [8]. Peer results agree: Avanti Feeds' Q2 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 19% year-over-year to Rs 16,097 Mn on shrimp processing and export volumes [4]. **The local data pack is supportive but not shrimp-specific** — Karnataka GST collections ran +11.1% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, and electricity demand +23.3% against +9.5% [D]. Treat that as a state tailwind, not proof of demand for your borrower's container. ## Who to pursue, and how to grow safely
**Pursue processors with their own tested ice and water, two or more export markets, and a named overseas buyer relationship.** Sandhya Aqua's US buyer AZGI takes only about 25% of its requirements from the company, which the rating treats as growth headroom [11] — that is the profile to back. **Avoid single-buyer units, tanker-water ice users, and anyone with working-capital utilisation near the ceiling.** Structure as a cash-flow-backed working-capital line with a packing-credit sub-limit, and take stock and book-debt statements every month, plus the water test report and buyer-wise shipment data. **The local press says little about Mangaluru's shrimp economics specifically** — the harbour coverage is political, not financial [3] — so lean on the peer and rating evidence above. - **Ice or water test failure at the harbour units** [1][2] — trigger a stop on new limits until the borrower produces a clean lab report. - **Realisation-led rather than volume-led growth in the borrower's numbers**, mirroring Apex's flat revenue [5] — trigger a re-cut of the projection on flat volumes. - **Buyer concentration above the Sandhya-Aqua-style 25% comfort band** [11] — trigger a covenant requiring a second market within two seasons.
